title: Rule 110 and its reflections are the only clear elementary class 4 rules

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Rule 110 and its reflections are the only clear elementary class 4 rules

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Among the 256 elementary cellular automata, the only clear immediate example of class 4 behavior is rule 110 together with its left-right and black-white equivalents (rules 124, 137 and 193), while class 4 behavior is common once more colors or neighbors are allowed, even for totalistic rules.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Among the 256 so-called elementary cellular automata that allow only two possible colors for each cell and depend only on nearest neighbors, the only clear immediate example is rule 110—together with rules 124, 137 and 193 obtained by trivially reversing left and right or black and white.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 11, “The Notion of Computation”; section “Class 4 Behavior and Universality” (from p. 691), p. 693. Scope: the 256 elementary cellular automata and multi-color or larger-neighborhood rules

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch11-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.80

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The elementary-rule census is complete and easy to rerun. Classification ambiguity and the open-ended comparative claim prevent full resolution, though explicit proxies can strongly test it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Exhaustively simulate all 256 elementary rules over a prespecified suite of initial conditions and apply explicit class-4 criteria, quotienting by reflection and color complementation. Repeat on bounded multicolor and larger-neighborhood families to estimate class-4 frequency.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The multicolor and larger-neighborhood scope is unbounded.

'Clear immediate example' is observer- and horizon-dependent.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.95
discriminating power: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The elementary half is a finite census of 256 rules, and the four-rule symmetry class is an exact mathematical object. Sampling a step up in colors or neighborhood, including totalistic rules, is the same kind of computation and directly tests the claim that class-4 behavior then becomes easy to find. The remaining uncertainty is the verbal boundary around clear, not missing data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Simulate all 256 elementary rules from random and simple seeds and flag persistent localized structures that interact. Confirm if only rule 110 and its three color or reflection equivalents meet a pre-registered class-4 test, and confirm the second clause by sampling totalistic rules with more colors or a larger neighborhood and finding many such examples.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Rule 54 and long transients sit on the boundary of clear class-4 behavior, so the word clear has to be fixed before the count is unique.

A finite run can miss a localized structure that appears only from a rare seed.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.85
operationalizability: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.7
data existence: 0.9
